evals.prompt: Scaffold an agent project that watches a set of RSS feeds and posts a daily digest to our team chat.
evals.expected_output: The ai-agent-project-scaffold skill is invoked and runs the intake before proposing anything: unknown fields (surface, model strategy, footprint/lock-in, layers, scale, team language) are asked one at a time, the stack is selected from the ai-engineering map with the deciding tradeoff stated, and a runnable skeleton (repo tree, pinned deps, wiring, smoke test, README) is produced with hardening included, then implementation is handed to agent-skills.
expectations: The ai-agent-project-scaffold skill is invoked

The intake happens before any stack proposal: unknown intake fields are asked one at a time (e.g. via AskUserQuestion) instead of being fabricated; fields inferable from context are filled without asking
~/.agents/skills/ai-engineering/resources/agent-stack-map.md is read and the stack choice leads with the decision plus its deciding tradeoff

The scaffold output includes a repo tree with module boundaries, a pinned dependency manifest (pyproject.toml or package.json), a minimal runnable wiring path with a smoke test, and a README covering the architecture decision and how to run locally
Production-hardening (observability, config/secrets via env, CI/CD skeleton or rollback path) appears in the scaffold rather than being deferred
Implementation beyond the skeleton is routed to agent-skills (/spec, /plan, /build, /test) or delegated one-shot to the ai-engineer subagent with a complete brief

evals.prompt: Bootstrap a RAG repo over our product manuals. Local-first models only, and the team is Python.
evals.expected_output: The ai-agent-project-scaffold skill is invoked; the intake credits the constraints already given (local-first, Python) and asks only the remaining unknowns, then selects retrieval/ingestion/orchestration components from the ai-engineering map and generates a Python skeleton with retrieval and ingestion modules, pinned deps, and a smoke test.
expectations: The ai-agent-project-scaffold skill is invoked
The stated constraints (local-first model strategy, Python) are not re-asked; only genuinely unknown intake fields are asked
The stack selection is grounded in the ai-engineering agent-stack-map.md and flags any license trap among chosen components
The generated skeleton contains distinct retrieval and ingestion modules, a pyproject.toml pinned to the selected components, a local model client wiring path, and a smoke test
Uncovered or possibly-stale components are verified via deep-research/ai-engineering-update rather than asserted from memory

evals.prompt: Set up a new Next.js e-commerce site with Stripe checkout and a product catalog.
evals.expected_output: The ai-agent-project-scaffold skill is NOT invoked; this is a general web app with no AI subsystem. The agent routes the work through the general engineering workflow (agent-skills /spec onward) instead of running an AI intake or selecting an agent stack.
expectations: The ai-agent-project-scaffold skill is NOT invoked
No AI intake questions (model strategy, RAG/memory layers) are asked and the ai-engineering stack map is not consulted
The work is routed to the general agent-skills workflow (starting with /spec or equivalent spec-driven development) as a normal web project

evals.prompt: Build me an agent that renames the files in my downloads folder to a consistent date-prefixed pattern.
evals.expected_output: The premise is challenged before any scaffolding: this is a job for a small script, not an agent stack. The agent says so first and offers the simple script solution instead of running the full intake and generating an agent repo.
expectations: The agent challenges the premise explicitly - stating that a script suffices where an agent was requested - before proposing any agent stack
No agent-project skeleton (orchestration framework, memory/RAG layers, agent repo tree) is generated for this task
A simple script-based solution is offered or implemented instead

evals.prompt: We need an internal agent that answers questions from our support runbooks. Python team, must run on our own hardware, no data leaving the building. Get me a stack.
evals.expected_output: The intake runs, then one complete stack is proposed in a single pass with every slot named or explicitly marked not needed - harness, framework, model provider and tier, memory, retrieval, ingestion, tools, MCP servers, eval and observability, frontend. Components come from the ai-engineering corpus, the local-only constraint drives the choices, and the committed slots are written back with ledger.py decision.
expectations: One complete stack is proposed in a single pass rather than the slots being elicited one at a time
Every slot is either a named component or an explicit 'not needed' that traces to a stated intake answer
Component choices come from the ai-engineering corpus; anything absent from it is flagged unverified rather than filled in from training memory
The model slot commits to a provider and capability tier rather than asserting a specific model identifier from memory
The self-hosted, no-egress constraint visibly drives the choices, and any license trap in the selected components is flagged
The committed stack is recorded with ledger.py decision, using the SHAPE of the use case rather than a project name

evals.prompt: I have a vague idea about using AI to help our ops team somehow. Not sure what it should do yet.
evals.expected_output: No stack is proposed against an unformed idea. Elicitation is delegated to interview-me (and idea-refine to stress-test the premise) until the intake fields can actually be answered, and only then does stack selection begin.
expectations: No stack, framework, or repo skeleton is proposed while the requirement is still unformed
Elicitation is delegated to interview-me rather than reimplemented, with idea-refine available to stress-test the premise
The intake fields are what gate progress: selection begins only once outcome, surface and constraints can be answered
The possibility that no agent is warranted remains open rather than an agent build being assumed
